tasks.short: Review registration statistics and write registration policies with faculty.

steps.what: Build registration statistics from the enrolment census.
Review registration statistics that sit outside the usual band.
Consult faculty officials on what the statistics imply.
Draft registration policies from the consultation notes.

loop.input: Consultation notes and the outlier note
loop.output: A policy draft that states only what the notes agreed
loop.check: Administrator deletes any rule the consultation did not discuss
loop.stop: One draft. A course with no note is left out.
loop.why_not_simpler: The notes are prose from a meeting, not a policy form

steps.what: Publish the registration policies the administrator signed.

tasks.design: {BI} builds registration statistics from {LMS}. The administrator reviews the outliers and consults faculty officials. Policies are drafted from those notes and published from {CMS} only on the version the administrator signed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Statistics were copied into a slide, and the policy was written without the faculty conversation beside it.
tasks.enabler_now: The census is already structured, and a policy library can hold a version once a person signs it.
tasks.still_hard: The consultation with faculty officials, and what the policy should say.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator signs the policy. A chart does not.

ambition.what: Whether a course should close to further registration this week

tasks.altitude: The faculty consultation stays. Outliers are ready before it. A course closes only when the administrator says so, not when a band is crossed.

reach.task: Publish an operational statistic from a system of record
reach.learn: Which figures can be generated, and which still need a meeting before a rule changes

evidence.claim: Corlytics Clausematch keeps a versioned policy library, maps text to rules, and can summarise a regulatory document. It does not write this institution's registration policy.
Choosing a registration rule from a faculty conversation is a judgement. The statistic is only the input.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: registration statistics for the current term and the policies that come out of one consultation. Admissions requirements are a different task.
Structured fields: course id, places, registered count, band, policy clause. The student office produces the census. A course with no census line is omitted, not estimated.
Use the existing report and the document store before a custom policy tool. Staff monitoring is out of scope.
Crossing a band does not close a course. That remains the consultation.
unknowns: Who counts as a faculty official for this consultation.
Which policies must be published to students the same day.
Whether the census is already a trusted extract.
research_questions: Is the usual band written down, or only remembered from last year?

incremental.description: Refresh the usual-band marks on registration statistics

approvals.approved_version: registration policies the administrator signed after consulting faculty
published copy of those signed registration policies

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the census is late and the consultation rewrites the draft. High: outliers are few and the draft is a short edit. The consultation stays. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with academic staff on admission and credit policies.

steps.what: Gather current admission requirements and course credit rules.
Confer with academic staff on admission requirements.
Draft the course credit policies the staff discussed.

loop.output: A draft limited to requirements and credit rules the notes record
loop.check: Administrator removes any requirement the notes do not contain
loop.stop: One draft. Silence in the notes is not a new rule.
loop.why_not_simpler: The conference is unstructured talk, not a form

steps.what: Adopt the admission requirements and the credit policies.

tasks.design: Current admission requirements and course credit rules are gathered from {DOCS}. The formulation happens in the conference with academic staff. The administrator adopts the text, and that adopted version is the one staff can read.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements lived in old mail, and the conference had no single text in front of it.
tasks.enabler_now: The current texts can be pulled into one pack, and a draft can follow the notes.
tasks.still_hard: The conference itself, and the judgement of what to adopt.
tasks.human_edge: Academic staff and the administrator formulate the rule. A draft does not adopt it.
tasks.altitude: The conference still takes the time. The pack is current when it starts. Adoption stays with the administrator.

reach.task: Agree a requirement with the people who must apply it
reach.learn: Which sentences can be drafted from notes, and which need the room

evidence.claim: GDPR Article 22 names admission decisions, and AI Act Annex III 3(a) names admissions. A requirement that decides admission is not adopted by automation alone.
A versioned policy library can store the adopted text. The conference still chooses the wording.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one conference on admission requirements and course credit policies, through to adoption. Individual admission recommendations are a different task.
Structured fields: requirement id, credit rule id, note id, adopted or not. The document owner produces the current text. A topic the notes do not cover is not drafted as a rule.
Use the document store before a custom policy tool. Test that configuration before any new screen.
unknowns: Which academic staff must be in the conference.
Whether adopted credit rules apply mid-year or next intake.
Who may adopt if the administrator chairs but does not vote.
research_questions: Are the current requirements a single controlled text?

incremental.description: File the adopted requirements where academic staff can read the current version

approvals.approved_version: admission requirements and credit policies the administrator adopted after the conference

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the conference reopens settled rules and the draft is rewritten. High: the pack is current and adoption is a short read. The conference stays. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select scholarship recipients and distribute aid under published rules.

steps.what: Load published rules for scholarship, fellowship and loan programs.
Mark files that fail a published rule of the programs.
Summarise eligible files before selecting recipients.

loop.input: An eligible application and the published rule table
loop.output: A short summary of facts the file states
loop.check: Administrator removes any sentence that recommends an award
loop.stop: One pass per file. A missing figure stays blank.
loop.why_not_simpler: Personal statements are prose, so a table cannot hold them

steps.what: Begin selecting scholarship and fellowship recipients.
Authorise the list before distributing aid.
Start distributing aid from the authorised payment list.

tasks.design: Published rules for scholarship, fellowship and loan programs sit in {DOCS} and {ERP}. A file that fails a published rule is marked, and the administrator selects recipients from the rest. {ERP} pays from {BANK} only after the administrator authorises that list, inside the delegated limit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Eligibility was rechecked by hand, and the payment list was retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: A published numeric rule can be applied to structured fields, and a payment file can be built from an authorised list.
tasks.still_hard: Selecting recipients when more people qualify than the program can fund.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator selects and authorises. A failed published rule is not an award decision.

ambition.what: Part-time students who meet a published rule see that eligibility before the panel meets

tasks.altitude: The panel still selects. Clearly ineligible files are marked first. Payments above the delegated limit leave this task.

reach.task: Select recipients for a limited support fund
reach.learn: Which eligibility checks are published rules, and which awards stay a panel

evidence.claim: GDPR Article 22 names scholarship decisions: they must not rest on automation alone, and the person must be able to contest them.
A published eligibility rule can be coded. A scarce award among people who all qualify is a panel judgement.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one round of scholarship, fellowship and loan programs, from rules to payment of the authorised list. Fundraising the money is a different task.
Structured fields: program id, published rule, pass or fail, recipient, amount. The program owner maintains the rule text. A rule that is not numeric is not auto-marked.
Use the finance and document systems already in place before a custom award tool.
A second finance signature, if the amount is above the administrator's delegated limit, sits outside this task. The payment does not run without the authorised list.
unknowns: The delegated limit for a single payment.
Whether loan programs use the same list as scholarships.
Who contests a mark that a published rule failed.
research_questions: Are eligibility rules stored as fields, or only as a PDF?

incremental.description: Keep published eligibility rules and the delegated payment limit current

approvals.approved_version: recipient decision the administrator made from eligible files
payment list the administrator authorised within the delegated limit
payment run generated from that authorised list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most files need a judgement and the panel is long. High: many files fail a clear published rule and the list is a check. Selection and authorisation stay. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take part in fundraising and encourage alumni participation.

steps.what: Pull the alumni list for institutional fundraising.
Draft a briefing for the fundraising activities.

loop.input: The checked contact list and the gift history on each record
loop.output: A briefing that uses only those fields
loop.check: Administrator removes any ask the record does not support
loop.stop: One pass. A missing history is left blank.
loop.why_not_simpler: The ask depends on a relationship, which is not a template paragraph

steps.what: Participate in the institutional fundraising event.
Encourage alumni participation by phone or visit.
Record the gift agreed during fundraising activities.

loop.input: Notes of what the alumnus agreed
loop.output: A gift note that states only that agreement
loop.check: Administrator edits the amount and the purpose before it is sent
loop.stop: One draft. No amount is invented.
loop.why_not_simpler: The agreement is a conversation, not a fixed pledge form

tasks.design: {CRM} holds the alumni list the administrator is allowed to contact. A briefing is drafted for the administrator to edit. The event, the ask, and the gift note stay with the administrator, and {EMAIL} sends a gift note only after that edit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lists were exported by hand, and a gift was written down differently from the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: A contact list with a recorded basis can be filtered, and a note can be drafted from the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Being at the event, and encouraging a particular person to take part.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator makes the ask. A list does not.

ambition.what: Which alumni to visit this quarter, from a list that has a recorded contact basis

tasks.altitude: Events and calls still take the week. The list is checked first. A gift is recorded only as the conversation left it.

reach.task: Ask a known party for a commitment and record what was agreed
reach.learn: Which preparation is a list, and which sentence has to be said by the person

evidence.claim: Encouraging alumni to take part is a relationship. The event and the call stay with the person who asks.
A gift note that states a different amount from the conversation is a worse record than no note.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one fundraising activity, the alumni asked to take part, and the gift note from that activity. Investing the gift is out of scope.
Structured fields: alumnus id, contact basis, last gift, note of agreement. The alumni office maintains the basis. A person with no recorded basis is not put on the list.
Use the contact register already in place before a custom fundraising tool. The lawful basis for contacting alumni is confirmed outside this task, not assumed.
No automated decision is made about an alumnus. The ask is a conversation.
unknowns: Which alumni the institution may contact, and on what basis.
Who may send a gift note in the institution's name.
Whether a verbal pledge is recorded before money arrives.
research_questions: Is the contact basis stored on the alumni record, or only implied by an old event list?

incremental.description: Keep the alumni contact basis and the visit list current

approvals.approved_version: gift note the administrator edited to match the conversation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the event and the calls dominate, and gifts are negotiated one by one. High: the list is clean and the note is a short edit. The ask stays. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Registration outliers, the current rule pack, eligibility marks and a checked alumni list arrive first. Faculty consultations, the award panel and the fundraising ask stay. Policies, recipients and gift notes go out only on a version the administrator has signed.
reach: Compliance managers can reuse a conference pack, not the credit rule the room adopts
Social and community service managers can see which aid files fail a published rule before a panel
skills_to_grow: Closing a course to registration only after the faculty consultation
Authorising a payment list inside the delegated limit
Leaving an alumnus off the ask list when no contact basis is recorded
role.ambitious_version: Every registration policy, aid payment and gift note matches a decision the administrator has already signed.
